preheader: Anthropic's massive IPO filing, Wall Street's record bonuses, and more top news.

lead.headline: Anthropic files for an IPO that could raise up to $64.4 billion
lead.body: The company behind the Claude AI assistant has revealed draft prospectus details for a public market debut. The offering aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion at an indicative price of $70 to $78 per share, setting up what could be an unprecedented test for public tech valuations.
lead.why: This is a massive benchmark for tech valuations and institutional investor appetite. If you are looking at tech investing or valuation multiples in your finance classes, this is the biggest case study of the year.

stories.headline: Wall Street bonus pool projected to jump 20% to 30%
stories.body: Big bank trading desks are on track for record profits and the fattest bonus haul in history. Hottest desks are seeing performance-related pay spike significantly.
stories.why: Good context for understanding compensation trends if you are eyeing high-finance or trading internships down the line.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares edge higher as fallout from CEO affair continues
stories.body: Nvidia stock saw pressure and faced a shareholder class-action lawsuit following reports regarding CEO Jensen Huang. The company lost billions in market value as the market weighed the corporate governance implications.
stories.why: A stark reminder of 'key-man risk' in corporate governance, showing how deeply a founder's personal actions can sway massive market valuations.

stories.headline: Crunchbase report shows AI taking nearly two-thirds of venture funding
stories.body: Venture capital is heavily concentrated in AI, capturing 64% of global venture dollars in the third quarter. Out of $159 billion total, AI startups pulled in $102 billion.
stories.why: This concentration dictates where early-stage capital flows, which matters if you want to launch a startup or work in venture capital.

stories.headline: McKinsey report says AI could cut manual banking risk tasks by up to 70%
stories.body: A new McKinsey study highlights that artificial intelligence can eliminate a large portion of manual operational tasks in bank risk functions. This shift aims to free up capacity for deeper strategic decision-making.
stories.why: As you study business and look at financial services, understanding how AI automates entry-level operational work will shape what junior roles actually look like.

stories.headline: Gen Z founders bypass traditional entry-level jobs to build AI startups
stories.body: A growing number of young people are skipping traditional corporate entry-level jobs to start their own companies. Lower software and operational costs driven by AI are making it easier to launch early-stage ventures.
stories.why: Directly relevant if you are weighing the traditional corporate recruiting track against building your own venture straight out of Merage.

stories.headline: University of California launches $38.2 million climate research initiative
stories.body: The Climate Change Research & Policy Institute was established to drive research across multiple campuses, including UC Irvine, UCLA, UC Santa Barbara, and UC Davis.

stories.headline: Ben Shelton agrees to massive new New Balance contract
stories.body: Following his US Open final run, 24-year-old tennis star Ben Shelton has signed a deal worth up to $18 million per year with New Balance, parting ways with On.

term.name: Key-Man Risk
term.definition: Key-man risk is the danger to a company's operations and stock price if a single vital executive, like a charismatic founder or CEO, suddenly leaves, faces a scandal, or can no longer lead. We saw this play out when Nvidia shares wobbled and investors scrambled following headlines about CEO Jensen Huang.

serve.headline: Snapp raised $4.6 million from a16z Speedrun to build a specialized sports prediction AI
serve.body: San Francisco-based Snapp secured backing to build an AI model tailored specifically for the speed and unpredictability of sports like football and basketball. General-purpose models struggle with live sports data, so Snapp is targeting that vertical gap.
